data.title: Honghe Technology Block Trade Totals 2.6268 Million Shares, 309 Million Yuan
data.description: Honghe Technology recorded a block trade of 2.6268 million shares on September 15, with turnover of 309 million yuan, according to Jiemian News. The trade accounted for 6.31% of the day's total turnover, was priced at 117.6 yuan per share, and represented a 14.92% discount to the market close of 138.23 yuan.

data.title: Brazil’s Smaller Iron Ore Miners Cut Output as Shipping Costs Surge
data.description: Smaller Brazilian iron ore producers are struggling with soaring shipping costs to top consumer China, squeezing margins and prompting production cuts, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Nvidia GeForce RTX 60 Series Expected in First Half of 2027
data.description: Nvidia's GeForce RTX 60 series, built on the Rubin architecture, is expected to launch in the first half of 2027. According to ChainCatcher, the new lineup may face supply constraints similar to the RTX 50 series, and retail prices could exceed the official suggested price.

data.title: Sri Lanka Growth Falls Short as Higher Oil Prices Weigh on Outlook
data.description:
Sri Lanka’s economy expanded less than forecast last quarter as elevated oil prices from renewed hostilities in the US-Iran war clouded the recovery outlook, according to Bloomberg.

The article said the island nation’s growth slowed from expectations, with the Middle East crisis adding pressure through higher energy costs.

data.title: Li Ning Founder Raises Stake To 20.25% After Buying Shares
data.description:
Li Ning founder Li Ning increased his stake in Li Ning Co. (2331) after buying 6.225 million shares on Sept. 9 and 1.295 million shares on Sept. 11, according to Ming Pao.

The shares were bought at average prices of HK$13.37 and HK$12.92, respectively. His holding rose from 19.96% to 20.25%.

data.title: BOC Hong Kong To Launch New Cross-Border Remittance Service On September 27
data.description:
BOC Hong Kong (2388) said it will launch its new personal cross-border remittance service, BOC Instant Remit, on September 27, according to Ming Pao.

The service is part of a retail cross-border payment innovation project jointly launched by SWIFT and banks. It will offer individual customers 24/7 cross-border remittances that take only a few minutes, the bank said, adding that the service is designed to remove the time and cross-time-zone limits of traditional transfers and make overseas fund transfers more convenient and efficient.

data.title: STOCKS | Tencent Sees HK$2.477 Billion Northbound Turnover On Shanghai Connect
data.description:
Tencent (00700) saw Northbound trading turnover jump to HK$2.477 billion in the Shanghai Connect, with net selling of HK$637 million, according to ETNet.

Hua Hong Semiconductor (01347) returned to the Shanghai Connect top 10 turnover list for the first time in several days, with Northbound investors buying HK$354 million and selling HK$833 million, for net selling of HK$478 million. China Gold International Resources (02099) and Tracker Fund of Hong Kong (02800) also re-entered the Shenzhen Connect top 10 turnover list for the first time in several days.

data.title: Keeper Expands Beyond TON to Support Seven Blockchain Networks
data.description: Keeper has rebranded from Tonkeeper and expanded its wallet support beyond TON to seven blockchain networks. According to NS3.AI, the wallet now supports TON, Bitcoin, Ethereum, TRON, BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum, and Base. The change follows TOP's assumption of the wallet's operational leadership last month.

data.title: Essity Prepares Consumer Tissue Exit Through Sale or Listing
data.description:
Essity AB is preparing to start a sales process for its consumer tissue business as soon as next month, according to people familiar with the matter, Bloomberg reported.

The Swedish company is weighing a sale or a listing for the unit after activist investor Cevian Capital took a minority stake.

data.title: Global Dividends Rise 7.3% In Q2, Janus Henderson Says
data.description:
Global dividends rose 7.3% year on year to $757.8 billion in the second quarter of 2026, while share buybacks also remained strong, according to ETNet.

Janus Henderson's latest Global Dividend Index showed Asia-Pacific companies excluding Japan paid $118.4 billion in dividends, up 6.4% in real terms. Japan posted one of the strongest dividend growth rates globally, with payouts of $52.6 billion, up 18.2%, and buybacks of $36.3 billion, ranking second among major markets.

Mainland China remained the largest dividend market in Asia-Pacific excluding Japan, with $61.8 billion in payouts, while Taiwan, South Korea, Australia and Hong Kong also recorded solid growth. Hong Kong companies paid $8.2 billion in dividends, up 4.3% in real terms, supported by AIA, Sands China and Galaxy Entertainment. Janus Henderson expects global dividend growth of 5% to 6% in 2026 and share buyback growth of about 7% to 8%.

data.title: STOCKS | Study Says BNPL Grocery Use May Push Up Prices for Everyone
data.description:
A new study says retailers are raising sticker prices as more consumers use buy now, pay later services, in part to widen margins and offset merchant fees. According to Sina Finance, the research found that about one in three shoppers in grocery checkout lines has used apps such as Klarna or Affirm to pay in installments for groceries and other essentials.

A LendingTree survey of more than 6,000 U.S. consumers in July found that 29% said they had used buy now, pay later loans to buy groceries, nearly double the 14% share from two years earlier. The study, led by Panos Kouvelis of Washington University in St. Louis, is scheduled to appear in the next issue of Management Science.

The researchers said retailers may raise prices and cut inventory because of the merchant fees charged on each buy now, pay later transaction. Kouvelis told Fortune that retailers accepting installment payments raise prices and that everyone ends up paying for the business model.

data.title: Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Stay in Profit for 30 Straight Days
data.description: Bitcoin short-term holders have remained in profit for at least 30 consecutive days, with $168.2 billion in coins in profit as of Tuesday. According to NS3.AI, $102.6 billion in short-term holder coins were still below their acquisition price. The broader Bitcoin investor base has stayed in net profit since Aug. 19.

data.title: Qantas to Retire All 10 Airbus A380s Starting in 2028, Four Years Earlier Than Planned
data.description: Qantas Group said it will gradually retire all 10 of its Airbus A380 aircraft starting in 2028, about four years earlier than previously planned, according to Jiemian News. The airline had originally planned to begin retiring the superjumbos in 2032 and replace them with more fuel-efficient Airbus and Boeing aircraft. Qantas said the decision was made because the delivery schedule for next-generation aircraft is "reassuring." It expects to save about A$300 million in net cash flow in fiscal years 2028 to 2031. The Airbus A380 entered service in 2007 and stopped production in 2021 after years of criticism over high fuel consumption, heavy maintenance costs and weak demand.

data.title: AI | Trustpilot CEO Says AI Search Demand Lifted Large Customers 35%
data.description:
Trustpilot Group Plc Chief Executive Officer Adrian Blair said demand from major brands seeking better visibility in artificial intelligence-powered searches helped drive a 35% increase in large customers on its platform in the first half, according to Bloomberg.

Blair made the comments as Trustpilot highlighted growing interest from brands in AI-powered search visibility.

data.title: Trump Administration Seeks Senate GOP Support for CLARITY Act
data.description:
The Trump administration is working to secure Senate Republican support for the CLARITY Act, while bank groups said Monday that recent revisions still do not make the stablecoin provisions acceptable. Some Republican senators, including John Cornyn of Texas, may side with banks and vote against the measure.

According to Foresight News, Cornyn said the latest text does not appear to address community banks' concerns about deposit outflows. The Council of Economic Advisers will launch an interactive tool on Tuesday that lets users set parameters and run scenarios to test its earlier conclusion that there is no significant link between stablecoin growth and community bank deposit outflows.

Patrick Witt, executive director of the President's Digital Asset Advisory Council, said the data show the banking lobby's deposit outflow narrative lacks support and that the bill includes safeguards for community banks. Democratic lawmakers also remain dissatisfied with the latest ethics language, saying it does not sufficiently restrict U.S. President Donald Trump and his family. Senator Adam Schiff said the provision does not effectively apply to the president and first family, while Mark Warner said the ethics language is far from adequate. Some Democrats are still negotiating changes before the vote.

data.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Endorses Final CLARITY Act Draft
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed the final CLARITY Act draft on Monday, saying the legislation is essential to helping the U.S. win the global race for new technology. According to NS3.AI, Bessent said the draft would give the Treasury Secretary new authority to respond if stablecoins cause substantial deposit outflows from community banks. The bill still lacks bipartisan consensus and needs 60 votes to pass.

data.title: STOCKS | Shanghai Composite Falls For Fourth Day As China Data Misses Demand
data.description:
China's Shanghai Composite fell for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, closing down 0.54% at 3,864.28, while the Shenzhen Component lost 0.72% and the ChiNext Index dropped 1.15%, according to ETNet.

Turnover in Shanghai and Shenzhen totaled RMB 1.6 trillion, the lowest this year and down RMB 16.5 billion from the previous session. Consumer-related sectors led declines, with tourism down 5.3%, while the semiconductor supply chain rose 1.6%.

Separately, the yuan's onshore spot rate closed at 6.7134 per dollar, its weakest since September 3, while the central parity rate was set at 6.7670, up for a fifth straight session and the strongest since February 3, 2023. ETNet also reported that China's industrial output growth accelerated in August, but retail sales growth slowed and fixed-asset investment fell more than expected.

data.title: Oil Prices Rise While Gold and Silver Fall
data.description:
October New York crude rose $2.26, or 2.23%, to $103.65 at 5:00 PM, while November Brent crude gained $1.86, or 1.84%, to $102.85, according to ETNet.

London gold fell $22.87, or 0.53%, to $4,265.34, and New York gold futures dropped $56.30, or 1.28%, to $4,352.60. London silver declined $0.29, or 0.46%, to $62.84, while New York silver futures lost $1.32, or 2.02%, to $63.87.

data.title: India’s August Trade Deficit Narrows as Oil Risks Persist
data.description:
India’s trade deficit narrowed in August even as instability across the Middle East and little sign the US or Iran are ready to back down added to economic headwinds, according to Bloomberg.

The report did not provide the size of the deficit or additional trade figures.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | BofA Says Fear of Disorderly Bond Yield Rise Is Cooling Risk Appetite
data.description: Exuberance in risk assets is fading as investors worry about a chaotic rise in bond yields and the results of US midterm elections, according to a survey by Bank of America Corp., Bloomberg reported.
